methods.label: Compare the two meeting intervals
methods.explanation:
At the first meeting, the girls have together covered half the track, because they started at diametrically opposite points and ran toward one another along a semicircle.

Between the first and second meetings, they start together and run in opposite directions. Their combined distance must reach one full track length before they meet again. This is twice their combined distance before the first meeting.

Their speeds are constant, so their combined distance grows at a constant rate. Therefore the time between the two meetings is twice the time from the start to the first meeting. Sally's distance also doubles between those intervals. Since she runs 150 meters between meetings, she ran
\[
150\div2=75
\]
meters before the first meeting.

Brenda and Sally therefore covered \(100+75=175\) meters together before the first meeting. This is half the track, so its length is
\[
2(175)=\boxed{350\text{ meters}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses meeting distances and direct proportion between time and distance at constant speed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is identifying the correct distance relationships for opposite-direction meetings. Direct proportion connects the half-lap and full-lap intervals, using distance equals speed times time. Basic circle terminology explains why diametrically opposite starting points give a half-lap initial separation.
